page: Microsoft Azure F2ads_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. Running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance features 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs with a high base clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 8.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance is equipped with a 236 GB NVMe SSD and is Premium Storage capable, though it does not include any GPU accelerators.

Performance benchmarks reveal strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression all ranking in the top tier. However, multi-core scaling is more moderate; stress-ng multi-core performance, PassMark CPU scores, and Redis SET operations fall into the average tier. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and static web serving throughput are weaker, landing in the bottom quarter of tested systems. Large-block memory bandwidth reads and writes also perform at average levels.

Given its dedicated high-frequency AMD EPYC cores and integrated local NVMe storage, the F2ads_v7 offers a cost-efficient profile for workloads requiring strong single-threaded execution without massive memory footprints. The primary tradeoff is the low core count, which limits multi-threaded scaling and makes it poor for demanding parallel tasks or medium-to-large language model inference. This instance is best suited for lightweight databases, single-threaded processing tasks, basic web serving, and general-purpose development or testing environments.
